stem:
Riya places a bar magnet on her study table and holds a steel paper clip near it. She then slides a thin sheet of cardboard between the magnet and the paper clip.
What will happen to the paper clip?

options.text: The paper clip is pushed away from the magnet.
The paper clip is still attracted to the magnet, because the magnetic effect passes through cardboard.
The paper clip falls, because any sheet placed in between completely blocks the magnetic effect.
The paper clip becomes a permanent magnet and sticks to the cardboard.

teacher.key_rationale: A magnetic effect acts across a gap and through non-magnetic sheets such as cardboard, so the steel paper clip remains attracted. Option C is the trap for learners who believe any intervening sheet blocks magnetism.
